Unit 9 • HL

Agents & Neural Computing

Introduction

Can we build a brain?

This unit explores AI that copies nature. You will investigate Reinforcement Learning (Training a dog with treats), Genetic Algorithms (Evolution and Survival of the Fittest), and Neural Networks (Mimicking the human brain's neurons).

You'll start by looking at Agents that learn from their environment. Then you'll simulate evolution with Genetic Algorithms. Finally, you'll look inside the 'Black Box' of Deep Learning and Convolutions (CNNs).

Reinforcement Learning (RL)

Learning by Trial and Error. Used in Robotics and Gaming.

  • Agent: The AI interacting with the world.
  • Environment: The world itself.
  • Reward: The feedback (+1 for good, -1 for bad).
  • Policy: The strategy the agent learns to maximize rewards.

Genetic Algorithms (GA)

Solving problems by evolving solutions over generations.

  • Fitness Function: Decides who survives (Survival of the Fittest).
  • Crossover: Mixing parents to create children.
  • Mutation: Random changes to prevent getting stuck.

Neural Networks (ANN)

Mathematical models inspired by biological brains.

  • Neuron: A math function that takes inputs, multiplies by weights, and fires.
  • Hidden Layers: The "thinking" layers between input and output.
  • Backpropagation: The learning process (correcting errors).

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)

Special AI for Vision (Images).

  • Convolution: Scanning an image with filters to find edges/features.
  • Pooling: Shrinking the image to focus on what matters.

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
AgentAn autonomous entity that perceives its environment and acts upon it.
Reward SignalFeedback from the environment that tells the agent how well it is performing.
Fitness FunctionA function that quantifies how close a given solution is to the optimum goal.
CrossoverCombining genetic information of two parents to generate new offspring.
MutationA random alteration in the genetic structure of an offspring.
Neural NetworkA network of artificial neurons used to solve complex problems.
WeightA parameter within a neural network that transforms input data within the network's hidden layers.
ConvolutionA mathematical operation that slides a filter over an input (image) to detect features.

Common Misconceptions

RL needs Teachers

Reinforcement Learning is NOT Supervised. There is no 'Correct Answer' key. The agent just knows if it got a treat or a shock.

Mutation is Bad

In Biology, maybe. In AI, Mutation is CRITICAL. Without it, the algorithm gets stuck in one solution (Local Optima).

Neural Nets 'Think'

They don't think. They are just giant multiplication machines fitting a curve to data.

  • A4.3.11 CNNs (Vision)

Real-World Uses

  • AlphaGo (Reinforcement Learning)
  • Antenna Design (Genetic Algorithms)
  • Face ID (CNNs)
  • Self-Driving Cars (Agents)
  • Video Game AI (RL)

Think Deeper

"The Ethics of Evolution" If we use Genetic Algorithms to design cars or buildings, and they evolve a solution we don't understand, can we trust it? Is 'It Works' good enough?
